description: SatHarvest is a project developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge to predict corn crop yields in Missouri. By combining NASA satellite data with Missouri agricultural records, we aim to understand how weather, soil conditions, and other factors affect corn production. Using data analysis and machine learning, our goal is to provide useful insights that can help farmers make better decisions and improve agricultural planning.
summary:
The goal of this project is to make the NASA weather data more useful for understanding historical patterns.
This project combines NASA POWER weather satellite data with Missouri agricultural records(USDA- United States Department of Agriculture).
 The project combines Python-based data processing, exploratory analysis, machine learning experiments, and an interactive web dashboard.

SatHarvest helps farmers, researchers, and students better understand how weather conditions relate to corn yields in Missouri. By combining NASA satellite-based weather data with agricultural records, the project makes historical weather and crop information easier to explore and analyze
details:
SatHarvest is a project that uses NASA weather and satellite data along with Missouri agricultural data to study and predict corn yields. We developed the project using Python and machine learning techniques and created an interactive dashboard to display the results. We also used Git and GitHub to manage our code.

Our main idea was to explore how NASA data can be used to address real agricultural challenges. By combining weather information with historical corn production data, we wanted to better understand how weather conditions affect crop yields. While developing the project, we focused on data quality, prediction accuracy, and making the results easy to understand.

What makes SatHarvest different is its focus on using space-based data to study corn production at the local level. We hope this project can serve as a starting point for further research and eventually help farmers and agricultural planners make better decisions. In the future, we would like to expand it to other crops and regions.
